'''Philip Marcus Levy''' (1934 – 2011) was a British psychologist who specialised in the field of [[mathematical psychology]].

==Life==
Phil Levy was born in 1934 in [[Redcar]], [[North Riding of Yorkshire]] but grew up in [[Leeds]] where he was a pupil at [[Leeds Grammar School]]. He took his first degree at the [[University of Leeds]] followed by a PhD on discriminant analysis at the [[University of Birmingham]] (1960). He stayed at Birmingham, initially as a research fellow and then as lecturer and senior lecturer. He was appointed the first chair in psychology at the [[University of Lancaster]] in 1972.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morris |first1=P. |title=Obituary - Philip Marcus Levy |journal=The Psychologist |date=2011 |volume=24 |issue=327}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldstein |first1=Harvey |title=Professor Phil Levy |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/professor-phil-levy-psychologist-who-aided-the-academic-expansion-of-his-discipline-2236079.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220526/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/professor-phil-levy-psychologist-who-aided-the-academic-expansion-of-his-discipline-2236079.html |archive-date=26 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |website=The Independent |accessdate=3 August 2020}}</ref>

He was active in the [[British Psychological Society]] and edited the [[British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology]]. He was elected  president of the society in 1978.  In his presidential address he called on psychologists to reflect on the assumptions underlying the science.  As he said: ''I feel that we have a simplified view of science, perhaps  due - for understandable sociohistorical reasons - for our anxious desire to receive the accolade of being 'scientific' [...] I believe that science is much more a matter of social exchange than many of us are prepared to admit.''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Levy |first1=Philip |title=On the relation between method and substance in psychology |journal=Bulletin of the British Psychological Society |date=1981 |volume=34 |pages=265–270}}</ref>

==Work==
His expertise was in mathematical and statistical psychology. He was an expert in the construction of tests in education and training.<ref>{{cite web |title=Obituary - Philip Levy |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/philip-levy-bhc55qtcbqh |website=The Times |access-date=3 August 2020}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1977-1978 - President, [[British Psychological Society]]
